_about: RATIFIED Company Standard DATA-LOSS-EXCLUSION-MSA-001 (AM-163, 2026-10-19). The position is the
manager's statement of the company's intended data-loss exclusion, recorded verbatim in Legal
Constitution L1.14 section 9 (owner instruction, 2026-10-19: match it to the Constitution, update it
if absent). It is CONFIGURATION: no locked decision is amended by this file.
PRESENCE Requirement: it verifies that the provision EXISTS. A clause in which the provider takes
RESPONSIBILITY for data loss is read as a waiver of the position (AM-152), so it is a DEVIATION and a
person decides. The position's caveat is part of it: subject to applicable law and legal review;
Counsel must reconcile it with confidentiality, personal-data protection and other liability
exceptions; it must not be treated as excluding liabilities that cannot lawfully be excluded.
description: The provider is not liable for loss, deletion, corruption or unavailability of customer data, or its restoration costs, whether direct or indirect.
source_document: Legal Mind — Legal Constitution, Lawyer Review Version L1.14 (docs/02-legal-domain/LEGAL_CONSTITUTION_L1.14.md)
source_clause: §9 Liability — Data-Loss Exclusion and Relationship to the Liability Cap
source_quote: Leapswitch/CloudPe shall not be liable for loss, deletion, corruption or unavailability of customer data, or associated restoration, recovery, reconstruction or recreation costs, whether those losses or costs are direct, indirect, incidental, special or consequential.

_terminology: Mapping terminology, ratified with the standard on 2026-10-19. Every term is drawn from the
Constitution's own wording of the position or names the clause type generically; no term encodes
a legal position (rules 7/21): the position lives in `configuration.expected_presence`, sourced
above. confirm_threshold 5 is STRUCTURAL: one exact phrase confirms; an alias or keyword group
scores 3, so two independent signals are always required. Waiver patterns are the provider
ACCEPTING the responsibility the position excludes — they are polarity terminology (35.4), and
none contains a negation, so "shall not be liable for data loss" is never one.
